textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE Giardia lamblia trophozoite (the binucleate flagellated gut parasite), shown from a three-quarter ventral angle so both the body shape and the flat underside are readable, centered and large in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around it for later labels. House style: semi-flat vector-style shading with THIN, CRISP, CLEAN dark outlines (never heavy black cartoon strokes), every structure carrying its own DISTINCT, CLEARLY READABLE soft colour fill with gentle soft shading - refined and elegant, not washed-out, not pastel-faded. Muted, sophisticated, slightly desaturated educational palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours) on a neutral dark charcoal uncluttered background that fills the frame edge-to-edge - no border, no frame, no vignette, no sheet lying on a surface.

BODY SHAPE - this is the whole point of the picture, get it exactly right: the cell is BILATERALLY SYMMETRIC, a teardrop or pear outline, broad and rounded at the front (anterior) end and tapering to a point at the back (posterior) end. The dorsal (upper/back) surface is smoothly CONVEX and domed; the ventral (lower/front-facing) surface is FLAT to gently CONCAVE, like the underside of a shallow boat or a flattened pear cut lengthwise. Warm translucent ivory-tan cytoplasm fill.

REQUIRED STRUCTURES, all clearly separated and labellable:
1. TWO NUCLEI as a mirror-image pair side by side near the broad anterior end, symmetric either side of the body's long midline - soft violet-blue ovals, each with a small deeper indigo dot (the karyosome) at its centre, together giving the whole cell a distinctive face-like look (like two eyes). Exactly two, never one, never asymmetric.
2. The VENTRAL ADHESIVE DISC on the flat underside: a large, clearly concave, spiral-ridged muted teal-grey structure occupying most of the anterior-to-mid ventral surface, like a shallow suction cup with visible spiralling microtubule ridges inside it - show it via the cutaway so its concave, sucker-like form and internal spiral structure are unmistakable.
3. The MEDIAN BODY: a curved, claw-hammer-shaped bundle of microtubules, dusty rose colour, lying on the midline toward the rear half of the cell, dorsal to where the tail-end flagella originate.
4. EIGHT FLAGELLA in FOUR bilateral pairs, pale amber-cream, thin and whip-like, each pair symmetric left/right: an ANTERIOR pair emerging near the front between/beside the nuclei and curving alongside the body, a POSTEROLATERAL pair emerging mid-body and trailing backward along the sides, a VENTRAL pair emerging from the disc region and trailing along the underside, and a CAUDAL pair emerging together from the tapered posterior tip and trailing free behind it. Count must read as exactly eight - four pairs, symmetric, distinguishable by where they emerge.

Do NOT draw: a single nucleus; asymmetric nuclei; an amoeba shape with pseudopods; a dense fuzzy coat of short cilia all over the surface; a bacterial cell wall or nucleoid; a virus capsid; prominent classical mitochondria; more or fewer than eight flagella; the disc on the dorsal instead of ventral surface; a flat 2D silhouette with no dorsal/ventral distinction. Anatomically faithful, single specimen only, no duplicates. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.
sem:
Photorealistic false-colour scanning electron micrograph (SEM) of a SINGLE Giardia lamblia trophozoite, three-quarter view showing both the domed back and enough of the flat underside to see the adhesive disc region, centered in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame and filling most of it, with an even margin and a perfectly uniform dark background of even tone - no border, frame, vignette, letterbox bar or corner darkening. The specimen rests on a subtly textured neutral substrate, crisp three-dimensional surface texture, shallow depth of field, cool studio microscopy lighting.

BODY SHAPE: bilaterally symmetric, a smooth teardrop/pear outline, broad rounded anterior end tapering to a point at the posterior end, dorsally convex and domed, ventrally flat with a shallow concave depression toward the front where the adhesive disc sits (visible as a sucker-like scalloped depression with faint spiralling ridges even under the false-colour surface rendering, not sharply cut open - SEM shows surface only).

Surface false-colour palette matching this microbe's legend: warm pale gold/tan across most of the body surface, with the concave disc region shaded a slightly cooler muted teal-grey so its shape reads clearly, and a subtle violet-blue tint suggesting the paired nuclei bulging gently just under the surface near the broad anterior end (visible as two symmetric low domes, not as an opened interior - SEM is surface topology only).

FLAGELLA: EIGHT thin, pale amber-cream whip-like flagella emerging in four bilateral, symmetric pairs - anterior pair near the front, posterolateral pair trailing from mid-body sides, ventral pair trailing from the disc region, and caudal pair trailing together from the tapered posterior tip - some may curve or loop naturally near the body as real flagella do, but all eight must ultimately be distinguishable as individual strands, not fused into a single thick cord and not so tangled that the count is unreadable.

Do NOT render: internal cutaway structures (SEM is surface-only, correct not to show the median body or an opened disc); a dense short ciliate fuzz; a bacterial wall; a virus capsid; more or fewer than eight flagella; pseudopods; pigment blotches unrelated to the described tints. Single specimen only, no duplicates, no cluster, no extra floating debris beyond faint out-of-focus specks in the background. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks anywhere in the image.
